question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Q2 FY27 call CFO Kress said gross margins would bottom in Q4 FY27 at roughly 71-72% (reportedly GAAP and non-GAAP alike), down from the 74.0% Q3 guide, because of memory costs, with 72-73% in FY28 once negotiated price increases land. NVIDIA's mid-quarter margin hints have historically come close to the later formal guide, so the median is at the midpoint, 71.5%. Downside risk: memory prices 'headed even higher' than expected, purchase commitments of $279B, possible conservatism under the interim CEO, and GAAP guides sometimes 0.1-0.2pt below non-GAAP. Upside: Q3 margins look to be holding (Polymarket Q3 non-GAAP 73-75% at 0.86, thin volume; a near-miss contract, not an anchor). No market prices Q4 GAAP guidance directly.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 press release (Aug 26, 2026): Q3 FY27 guide revenue $108.0B +/-2%; GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% +/-50bp; Q2 non-GAAP GM was ~75% (MarketPulse preview, Nov 2026).
- Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026, per BigGo Finance and EffectStory recaps): CFO Kress said margins would 'bottom in the fourth quarter at roughly 71 per cent to 72 per cent', reportedly for both GAAP and non-GAAP; FY28 margins to settle at 72-73% as negotiated price increases take effect in Q1 FY28.
- Kress (Aug 2026, Dealroom/BigGo): memory price increases 'exceeded our prior expectations and are headed even higher into next year'; supply commitments rose from $119B to $279B, mostly memory; inventory $31.6B ahead of the Vera Rubin ramp.
- Investing.com scenario piece (Nov 2026): consensus Q4 revenue ~ $124.95B vs Q3 est ~$108.85B; gives no consensus Q4 GM figure; component costs flagged as a watch item.
- Context: Jensen Huang resigned; Kress is interim CEO; Nov 17, 2026 is the first report without Huang (Invezz, HeyGoTrade previews).
- Historical GAAP vs non-GAAP guide gap: often 0-0.2pt (e.g., Q3 FY26 guide GAAP 73.3% vs non-GAAP 73.5%); Q3 FY27 guide had both at 74.0%.
- Status quo: the guide is consistent with the stated 71-72% Q4 trough.
- Resolves off the midpoint of the GAAP gross margin guide in the 'Outlook' section of the Q3 FY27 press release, rounded to 0.1%; not the non-GAAP figure, not call commentary.
- Event window: release on 2026-11-17 after market close; as of 2026-11-17T00:10Z the release has not happened.
- Searched but not found: analyst consensus for Q4 GAAP GM; any human market on Q4 guidance (Polymarket contracts cover only Q3 non-GAAP actuals).

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the core facts: the Q2 FY27 call signaled a 71-72% Q4 trough, Q3 had GAAP=non-GAAP=74.0%, guides use 0.5pt steps, no Q4 market exists. Run 1 said the commentary was 'reportedly' GAAP and non-GAAP alike, while Run 2 said it was unclear; I can't settle this without web access, so I keep a small GAAP-downside skew. Remaining differences in tail width are judgment calls; I carry the runs' reference class and a dispersion between theirs.
